tickets.title: Launch facts: valid thinking per model, next place on a failed launch, worker HUD home
tickets.what: Starts after WORKER-MCP lands (same launch path). The model facts record which thinking levels each model supports (today only a boolean, src/roles/model-discovery.ts:21); every dispatch maps an unsupported level to the nearest supported one and names it; a place whose launch fails before the worker takes any input is skipped for that dispatch and hud_create tries the next place in the same call, returning the places tried; in worker mode the HUD home comes from the job directory, so worker tools work under Codex without HUD_HOME forwarded. Spec §2.1 (owner 2026-11-21). Proposal: oracle report j61e7649cba37181c A1, A2, A8.

acceptance.text: A sonic or imp dispatch with an unsupported thinking level launches with the nearest supported level and the result names it
A launch that fails before input falls through to the next available place in one hud_create call; the result lists the places tried and the real cause of each failure
Worker tools resolve the HUD home from the job directory when HUD_HOME is unset
Main-path tests for the three behaviours pass

tickets.title: Derived keys, repair of a closed job, one send to several jobs, retry_of
tickets.what: request_key and message_key become optional: the HUD derives them (hash of pane, role, cwd and task; job and text for a send), an explicit key still wins. hud_send to a job closed by a read creates the repair job itself with the earlier brief and report as references and returns continued_as. hud_send accepts jobs: [...] and sends only to working jobs, naming those skipped. hud_create({retry_of}) copies a failed job's brief and options onto the next available place. Proposal A3, A6, A7.

acceptance.text: hud_create and hud_send work without a key and a retry of the same call returns the same job or send
hud_send to a closed job returns continued_as with a new job whose brief references the earlier brief and report
hud_send with jobs sends once per working job and lists skipped jobs
hud_create with retry_of re-dispatches a failed job's brief on the next place
Main-path tests pass

tickets.title: Standing brief and a convention without per-harness delivery text
tickets.what: A registered project's .hud/brief.md is referenced in every local brief after the task (never before it: the opening lines feed tab labels and panel titles) and inlined, bounded, in browser briefs through the existing context block. The convention's per-harness delivery lines (hud-convention.md about lines 23-37) move into tool results as a hint for the caller's own harness; the server remembers it already sent the convention so the model no longer passes convention_version. Proposal A4, A5.

acceptance.text: A project with .hud/brief.md gets one reference line after the task in every local brief; tab labels are unchanged
hud_create and hud_roster results carry a delivery hint for the caller's harness only
The convention no longer describes Claude, Codex and pi delivery; a second hud_roster in the same session omits the convention without convention_version
Main-path tests pass

tickets.title: Leases for shared resources
tickets.what: Starts after WORKER-MCP (worker-mode tool list). hud_lease({name, release?}) in both modes: an exclusive file under $HUD_HOME/leases/ keyed by project root and name; the call waits a bounded time inside the caller's own turn and returns granted or held_by; a lease whose holder job is terminal or whose process is gone is reclaimed by the next caller. No resident process. Control shows a lease row (name, holder, waiting, age). Proposal B1.

acceptance.text: Two workers asking for the same lease: one is granted, the other gets held_by and is granted after release
A lease held by a closed or dead holder is reclaimed by the next caller
The main session can hold and release a lease
Control shows active leases
Main-path tests pass

tickets.title: Project scope and restart recovery
tickets.what: Jobs belong to a project, not a pane: hud_read({}) and changes are scoped to the caller's project root; a session in the same project adopts jobs whose recorded pane is gone (questions then reach the new session); after a machine restart, a worker that herdr resumed in the job's tab is recognised and kept rather than recorded as failed (seen 2026-11-21: herdr resumed a pi imp and a Claude oracle, HUD had failed both and reaped nothing). Proposal B4 plus restart recovery.

acceptance.text: hud_read({}) lists only the caller project's jobs
A new session in the same project receives questions and events of jobs whose pane is gone
A job whose worker herdr resumed after a restart is shown as working and settles normally
Main-path tests pass

comments.author: MCPORCH-05, 86754046
comments.text:
items 1, 2 and 4 landed. Item 3 (restart recovery) stopped under its stop rule:
after a reboot the watcher sees the dead supervisor and the old worker pid/start time and writes `failed: worker
exited`, while herdr relaunched the session with a new pid. herdr 0.9.5 exposes tab/pane ids, agent name and an
optional native session ref, but no proof that the process now in the pane is the job's worker with its settlement
hooks; pane ids are server-scoped and receipts do not pin the server. A follow-up needs the HUD to record the herdr
server and the native session id at launch and to reattach the lifecycle writer only on a matching session.

comments.author: RESTART-RECOVERY, job jed235679bed45e93
comments.text:
an isolated herdr 0.9.5 stop/start smoke showed resumed agents
keep their exact `agent_session`, name and tab (new pids), but lose `HUD_JOB_DIR`; pi restarts as `pi --session
<path>` without `--task-dir`, `--hud-worker-tools` or the HUD extension, Claude as `claude --resume <id>` without its
flags; `resume_argv` did not change that. So identity can be proven, but the worker protocol cannot be restored by
adopting the pid. Remaining option (owner decision): the HUD itself relaunches a recognised session with its bindings
(pi `--session <path>` + the launch contract and job env; Claude `--resume <id>` + job env) in the job's tab.

comments.author: owner decision
comments.text: option B, restarts stay manual. Item 3 is not built; the spec line now says so.

tickets.title: HUD-run checks bound to the report
tickets.what: hud_create({checks: [commands]}): after the worker declared the turn finished, a short-lived helper started by the on-demand watcher runs each command in the job's directory with a timeout and writes checks.json (exit code, duration, output tail, report signature). A new turn or rewritten report makes it stale. hud_read and the event line carry the result; the Inspector and job card show a check chip. Commands come only from the main session. Checks never settle, accept or fail a job. Proposal B3.

acceptance.text: A job with checks gets checks.json bound to its final report signature
A repair turn marks earlier check results stale
hud_read and hud watch show pass or fail per check
No resident process beyond the watcher and its short-lived helper
Main-path tests pass

tickets.title: MCP tasks for Claude Code (verify first)
tickets.what: Pulled forward from the M5 candidates (spec). First verify, in a real Claude Code session, how MCP tasks wake the session, cancel and show in /tasks; report before building. Then one task per worker turn (hud_create, hud_send, hud_respond) ending at a report or question; the result is state, report path and a one-line summary, not a read; cancel closes the job; such clients do not see hud_wait, hud watch, changes or watcher_alive. Removes the 30-minute Monitor re-arm.

acceptance.text: A written verification of Claude Code's wake, cancel and /tasks behaviour with MCP tasks
If verified: a Claude main session dispatches and is woken at report or question without hud watch
Main-path tests pass

Claude Code 2.1.330 ignores the

tickets.what: Settlement lines that arrive within a few seconds become one notice in hud watch and the other delivery paths (src/cli/watch.ts:20-21), so a large main-session context is woken once; questions stay immediate. Small.

acceptance.text: Three settlements within the window produce one notice naming all three
A question is delivered at once
Main-path test passes
